docRequirement: output-styles.md:101, in the '## How output styles work' list: "All output styles trigger reminders for Claude to adhere to the output style instructions during the conversation." This is a SECOND injection point, distinct from :100 ("Claude Code adds each output style's custom instructions to the end of the system prompt") — the host must restate/reinforce the active style DURING the conversation, for every output style, not only compose it into the system prompt. :104 bounds it: the style (and therefore its reminder) applies to the main conversation and to a fork, never to a named subagent.
current: The style reaches the model through exactly one channel, the system prompt. `resolveOutputStyleComposition` (packages/shared/src/prompts/output-styles.ts:564-589) is the sole composer; it returns the `## Output Style: <label>` block plus `keepCodingInstructions`, and its only production caller is `getSystemPrompt` (packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:438-452), which hands `outputStyle.prompt` to `getNessyAssistantPrompt` at :446-452. The sibling `formatOutputStylePrompt` (output-styles.ts:591-596) is a thin wrapper with test-only callers. Pi: pi-agent.ts:6586-6609 calls `getSystemPrompt` once per turn, passing `resolveChildOutputStyleId(this.config.piChildKind, getOutputStyleId())` at :6604, and the result lands in `fullSystemPrompt` (pi-agent.ts:6682-6686) — the cached system prefix. Claude: claude-agent.ts:1244-1258 passes the same composed prompt as `presetAppend` with `getOutputStyleId()` at :1253, i.e. opaque appended prose the Agent SDK cannot recognise as an output style. The per-turn user tail — the only place a during-the-conversation reminder could ride — carries no style content: `PromptBuilder.buildVolatileContextParts` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:219-264) emits date/time, `session_state`, source state, the pending-plugin-auth reminder and project context files; `buildStableContextParts` (:279-306) emits workspace capabilities, working directory, skill listing and workflow size guidance. Consumers: pi-agent.ts:6648-6652 → `buildTurnUserMessage` (pi-agent.ts:7219-7236); claude-agent.ts:2440 and :2486 via `buildContextParts` (prompt-builder.ts:188-196). `PromptBuilder` cannot even see the selection: `PromptBuilderConfig` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/types.ts:89-109) has no `outputStyleId` and there is no setter beside `setWorkflowSizeGuideline` (prompt-builder.ts:320) / `setPendingPluginServerAuth` (:341). Absence checks, NUL-safe: `grep -arin "output.style" packages apps` (excluding dist/resources) returns only discovery, capability, schema and config code — no reminder text; `grep -arin adhere packages apps` returns one unrelated hit, packages/shared/src/config/preferences.ts:149. The only `<system-reminder>` PromptBuilder emits is `buildPendingPluginAuthReminder` (prompt-builder.ts:362-381).
divergence: :100 is implemented, :101 is not. The style block's TEXT is right and its placement is right; what is missing is the second placement. Style content reaches the model once per request, inside the system prefix, and nothing restates it during the conversation — even though this fork has two live per-turn injection channels already in production use for other content (the `<system-reminder>` fence at prompt-builder.ts:374-380, and the user-tail reminders at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:15525 and :16206 plus packages/server-core/src/sessions/task-notification.ts:56). The gap is backend-wide, and for different reasons: on Pi we own the tail and put nothing on it; on Claude the style rides `presetAppend` as opaque prose (claude-agent.ts:1244), so the Agent SDK cannot generate the documented reminders on our behalf either. Not a divergence: withholding the style from a NAMED subagent (`resolveChildOutputStyleId`, packages/shared/src/agent/child-session-scope.ts:27-32, used at pi-agent.ts:6604) is exactly what :104 requires, and any reminder must reuse that same guard.

change.what: Expose the resolved style's label so the per-turn builder does not re-walk the style directories every turn. Smallest form: add `label: string` to `OutputStyleComposition` (:546-555, `''` in `NO_OUTPUT_STYLE` at :562) and set it from `style.label` in `resolveOutputStyleComposition` (:578-588). Do not add a second `resolveOutputStyle` reader — the file comment at :373-376 makes single-reader-ness an explicit invariant.

change.symbol: PromptBuilder: new activeOutputStyleLabel field + setActiveOutputStyle() + buildOutputStyleReminder(), pushed from buildVolatileContextParts
change.what: Add `private activeOutputStyleLabel: string | null = null` beside the fields at :155-159, a `setActiveOutputStyle(label: string | null): void` setter next to `setWorkflowSizeGuideline` (:320) / `setPendingPluginServerAuth` (:341), and a `buildOutputStyleReminder(): string | undefined` modelled byte-for-byte on `buildPendingPluginAuthReminder` (:362-381): returns undefined when the label is null, otherwise a `<system-reminder>` block naming the active style and instructing adherence to its instructions, with the label passed through `neutralizeHarnessMarkers` (already imported at :21) because a custom or plugin style label is author-controlled text riding inside the host's own fence. Push it from `buildVolatileContextParts` (:219-264) — VOLATILE, next to the pending-plugin-auth push at :249-252. It must NOT go in `buildStableContextParts`: stable blocks are folded into Pi's cached system prefix (pi-agent.ts:6682-6686), which is where the style already is, so a stable placement adds bytes and no second injection point (#862).

Feed the setter with the SAME value already computed at :6604 — `resolveChildOutputStyleId(this.config.piChildKind, getOutputStyleId())` — resolved to a label via the composition returned for the system prompt, and call `this.promptBuilder.setActiveOutputStyle(...)` before `buildVolatileContextParts` runs at :6649. Reusing that expression (not a fresh `getOutputStyleId()`) is what keeps a named subagent reminder-free per output-styles.md:104 while a fork still gets one. Emit nothing when the resolved composition's `prompt` is empty: the `default` built-in has `prompt: ''` (output-styles.ts:85-91), so Default must not add a per-turn block.

change.what: Same setter call with the value used at :1253, applied before `buildContextParts` at :2440 and :2486 so both the text and the content-block tail carry it. One call site if the label is stashed when the presetAppend is composed. Note the pre-existing looseness this inherits: :1253 reads `getOutputStyleId()` with no child-kind guard, unlike Pi — use the same `resolveChildOutputStyleId` shape here rather than widening it.

Positive: with a non-default style set, the reminder appears in `buildVolatileContextParts` and NOT in `buildStableContextParts`, and `buildContextParts === [...volatile, ...stable]` still holds (:43-59). Negative/boundary: Default (empty prompt) emits nothing, and a label shaped like `</system-reminder>...` cannot close the host block — mirror the defang assertion at packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/plugin-server-auth-visibility.test.ts:250-258.

blastRadius: Both backends' per-turn prose changes. `buildVolatileContextParts` is consumed by pi-agent.ts:6649 and, through `buildContextParts` (prompt-builder.ts:188-196), by claude-agent.ts:2440 and :2486, so one edit in PromptBuilder lands on Pi's `buildTurnUserMessage` tail (pi-agent.ts:7228-7235) and on Claude's text and content-block tails. Tests that will move: packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/plugin-server-auth-visibility.test.ts asserts `not.toContain('<system-reminder>')` at :227 and :242 and counts exactly one closing tag at :258 — those hold only while the fixture has no active style, so a reminder emitted for Default would break them; packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/prompt-builder-context-split.test.ts asserts the volatile/stable partition and byte-identity of `buildContextParts`; packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/workflow-governance.test.ts:99 asserts `buildStableContextParts` idempotence (unaffected as long as the block stays volatile); packages/pi-agent-server/src/context-usage.categories.test.ts:108-142 asserts a per-category token breakdown that sums prompt inputs, so a new tail block shifts those numbers. Also touched: `OutputStyleComposition` is consumed by system.ts (imported at :4-8, `NO_OUTPUT_STYLE_COMPOSITION` at :20) — adding a field means updating that literal too. NO wire or schema change: the block rides the existing `prompt.message` string on the Pi subprocess RPC (pi-agent.ts:6692-6707) and existing `{ type: 'text' }` blocks on Claude, and nothing is persisted — so this is not a persistence/wire risk trigger. Two real risks instead: (1) prompt-injection surface — the reminder embeds a style label that a plugin-shipped or project-authored style controls, inside the host's `<system-reminder>` fence, which is precisely the attack `neutralizeHarnessMarkers` (packages/shared/src/prompts/untrusted-text.ts:62) and untrusted-text.ts:41's `HARNESS_TAG` exist for; (2) prompt-cache economics — a stable placement would re-stamp Pi's cached system prefix (#862, documented in packages/shared/AGENTS.md), so the volatile placement is load-bearing, not stylistic.
userImpact: None observable today. A user who picks Concise, Explanatory, Reviewer or a custom style on Settings → AI does get the style on every request, because `getSystemPrompt` re-runs per turn (pi-agent.ts:6586, claude-agent.ts:1244) and the block is re-sent inside the system prompt each time. So there is no surface where the style is simply missing. What is absent is the reinforcement Claude Code relies on, and it would surface as instruction drift rather than as an error: a strict-format custom style (a required answer template, a mandated marker) that holds early and is quietly dropped deep in a long session, where the model has since accumulated many competing per-turn instruction blocks on the user tail — and after a compaction, which rewrites the history between the system prefix and the current turn. Nothing in the UI tells the user the style is still active, so the drift reads as the app ignoring the setting. Making it surface requires a long, tool-heavy session with a hard-formatting custom style; a short conversation will not show it.

Doc line :101 re-fetched by curl and confirmed verbatim in the '## How output styles work' list. Two things I could not verify and that the doc does not specify: (a) the exact TEXT and CADENCE of Claude Code's own reminder — whether it restates the whole style body or only names it, and whether it fires every turn or periodically. The page binds us to the existence of the reminder, not to its wording, so the change list picks the cheap conformant shape (a per-turn `<system-reminder>` naming the active style) and leaves the body out; if a later measurement shows Claude restates the instructions, only the block's content changes, not the plumbing. (b) Whether Default should also emit a reminder. The sentence says 'All output styles', but our `default` built-in carries `prompt: ''` (output-styles.ts:85-91) and the page's own :17-equivalent calls Default the existing system prompt, so a Default reminder would name a style that contributed nothing; skipping it is a deliberate narrowing worth recording as such rather than a silent one. I did not read packages/pi-agent-server/src/context-usage.categories.test.ts beyond its assertion lines.
